pairs: Post hæc rex Assuerus exaltavit Aman filium Amadathi,
After this, king Artaxerxes exalted Haman, the son of Hammedatha,
et posuit solium ejus super omnes principes quos habebat.
and he set his throne above all the rulers whom he had.
who passed by the doors of the palace,
for so the ruler had instructed them.
Only Mordecai did not bend his knee,
who presided over the doors of the palace, said to him,
Cur præter ceteros non observas mandatum regis?
“Why do you, more than the others, not observe the king’s command?”
And when they were saying this frequently,
and he would not listen to them,
scire cupientes utrum perseveraret in sententia:
desiring to know whether he would continue in his resolution,
dixerat enim eis se esse Judæum.
for he had told them that he was a Jew.
Now when Haman had heard this,
et experimento probasset quod Mardochæus non flecteret sibi genu,
and had proved by a test that Mordecai did not bend his knee to him,
et pro nihilo duxit in unum Mardochæum mittere manus suas:
And he considered it pointless to lay his hands on Mordecai alone,
audierat enim quod esset gentis Judææ;
for he had heard that he was part of the Jewish people.
to destroy the entire nation of the Jews,
who were in the kingdom of Artaxerxes.
in the twelfth year of the reign of Artaxerxes,
the lot was cast into an urn,
which in Hebrew is called Pur,
et quo mense gens Judæorum deberet interfici:
to determine on what day and in which month the Jewish people should be destroyed.
And it turned out to be the twelfth month,
And Haman said to king Artaxerxes,
Est populus per omnes provincias regni tui dispersus, et a se mutuo separatus,
“There is a people dispersed throughout all the provinces of your kingdom and separated one from another,
who make use of unusual laws and ceremonies, and who,
in addition, show contempt for the king’s ordinances.
et optime nosti quod non expediat regno tuo ut insolescat per licentiam.
And you know very well that it is not expedient for your kingdom that they should become insolent through independence.
declare that they may be destroyed,
et decem millia talentorum appendam arcariis gazæ tuæ.
and I will weigh out ten thousand talents to the keepers of your treasury.”
Tulit ergo rex annulum, quo utebatur,
And so the king took the ring that he used,
et dedit eum Aman filio Amadathi de progenie Agag,
and gave it to Haman, the son of Hammedatha, of Agag lineage,
And he said to him, “Let the silver,
which you promise, be for yourself.
de populo age quod tibi placet.
As for the people, do with them as it pleases you.”
Vocatique sunt scribæ regis mense primo Nisan,
And the scribes of the king were summoned, in the first month Nisan,
on the thirteenth day of the same month.
and to the judges of the provinces,
ut quæque gens legere poterat et audire pro varietate linguarum ex nomine regis Assueri:
so that each people could read and hear according to their various languages, in the name of king Artaxerxes.
And the letters were sealed with his ring.
missæ sunt per cursores regis ad universas provincias,
These were sent by the king’s messengers to all the provinces,
so as to kill and destroy all the Jews,
from children all the way to the elderly,
on the thirteenth of the twelfth month,
And the effect of the letters was this:
et pararent se ad prædictam diem.
and prepare for the prescribed day.
The couriers, who had been sent,
qui missi erant, regis imperium explere.
hurried to complete the king’s command,
but the edict was hung up in Susa immediately.
And the king and Haman celebrated a feast,
et cunctis Judæis, qui in urbe erant, flentibus.
while all the Jews in the city were weeping.
